mvp_scope.name: Source BlendR Launch MVP
mvp_scope.definition: A single workspace owner can discover and import products and services from vendor websites and PDF catalogs into a Discovery Session, review and import them into a Universal Catalog, search and filter that catalog, swap AI providers via adapter configuration, and use basic business outputs (flyer and quote PDFs) if time permits. Background workers keep the UI responsive. The platform fully operates with zero AI providers configured.
mvp_scope.rationale: Import-to-catalog flow, provider-agnostic AI, background processing, search/filtering, and simple pricing are the core differentiation. Flyer and Quote Builders are should-have and may be trimmed to MVP-minimal or deferred if risk grows. Analytics, memory, sync, integrations, and team features are deferred to future releases.

frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui-compatible component primitives
frontend.state: Server Components and server actions for standard flows; client state only for interactive discovery/catalog workflows

backend.framework: Next.js route handlers and server actions
backend.api_style: Route Handler -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma for REST-style JSON endpoints and app-owned mutations
backend.background_jobs: Separate TypeScript BullMQ worker on Redis for all long-running tasks

packages.packages/domain: Domain services, use cases, orchestration, business logic, and service interfaces consumed by web and worker.
packages.packages/ai: AI Capability Router, provider adapter interfaces, provider implementations, request/response normalization, and provider health checks.
packages.packages/scrapers: Playwright website discovery, navigation tree extraction, PDF/OCR import connectors, and raw artifact collection.
packages.packages/shared: Shared utilities, config helpers, logging, errors, constants, and cross-cutting primitives.
packages.packages/validation: Deterministic validation rules, duplicate checks, SKU/price/category rules, and candidate-to-catalog import gates.
packages.packages/types: Shared TypeScript types, DTOs, schemas, queue payloads, and API contracts.

domain_service_layer.request_flow: Route Handler / Server Action -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma -> PostgreSQL
domain_service_layer.worker_flow: BullMQ Processor -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma -> PostgreSQL
domain_service_layer.rule: Business logic lives in domain services and validation package, not directly inside route handlers, server actions, or queue processors.

database.search: PostgreSQL full-text search for MVP; external search deferred until scale evidence exists

storage.usage: PDF uploads, generated PDFs/PNGs, import snapshots, rendered DOM snapshots when retained

authentication.tenant_model: Workspace maps to Clerk organization and application workspace_id
authentication.authorization: Application-enforced RBAC with workspace_owner for MVP

hosting_and_deployment.workers: Fly.io TypeScript worker service with Playwright runtime
hosting_and_deployment.observability: Sentry plus structured logs and queue/job metrics

testing_stack.route_integration: Vitest against route handlers/server actions through domain services
testing_stack.worker_integration: Vitest against BullMQ processors through domain services
testing_stack.security: tenant-isolation integration tests and credential handling checks

ai_and_external_services.status: stable interface for all AI integrations

pipeline_architecture.scraping_pipeline: External source -> connector/scraper -> raw import artifact -> normalized source record -> Discovery Session candidate seed
pipeline_architecture.ai_enrichment_pipeline: Normalized source record or catalog candidate -> AI Capability Router -> Provider Adapter -> enrichment result -> validation -> candidate/catalog update
pipeline_architecture.separation_rule: Scraping collects and normalizes source data; AI enrichment is independently repeatable and can re-enrich stored normalized source records without re-scraping.
pipeline_architecture.re_enrichment_support: Persist normalized source records and import artifacts with version/source hashes so users can rerun enrichment after changing provider, prompt, capability route, or validation rules.

selected_stack.rationale: A Next.js full-stack monorepo with a separate BullMQ worker is the simplest scalable architecture: route handlers and server actions stay thin, all business logic is centralized in shared domain services, workers reuse the same domain services, scraping and AI enrichment remain independent pipelines, and the AI Capability Router/Provider Adapter interface remains stable for all AI integrations.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Too risky for Playwright/OCR/AI jobs; workers must scale and run independently.
Adds a second language while frontend, Playwright, and worker ecosystem remain TypeScript-heavy.
Over-engineered before scale evidence; monorepo packages plus separate worker are enough.
Unnecessary until catalog scale proves PostgreSQL full-text insufficient.

development_roadmap.strategy: Foundation then demonstrable vertical slices, with risky integrations proven before release hardening.

phases.name: Execution foundation
phases.goal: Create the selected-stack monorepo, shared contracts, tenant boundary, data schema, queue, and UI foundation.
readiness_criteria: Clerk organization maps to workspace context
App shell and design tokens render responsively

phases.name: Catalog and provider baseline
phases.goal: Deliver vendor/catalog/manual workflows and provider routing before risky ingestion paths.
readiness_criteria: Manual item path works with zero AI providers
Provider health and routing states are visible

phases.name: Import-to-discovery vertical slices
phases.goal: Deliver website and PDF imports through observable jobs into the review-first Discovery Session.
readiness_criteria: Website and PDF inputs create idempotent jobs
Partial failures and retries are visible
Bulk outcomes are per-record and recoverable

phases.name: Release hardening
phases.goal: Close security, accessibility, integration, observability, and rollout gates.
readiness_criteria: Tenant isolation and credential checks pass
Responsive and keyboard evidence is registered
Rollback and operational checks are rehearsed

implementation_sequence.approach: Foundation-first, then vertical slices with contract gates

technical_prerequisites.dependency: packages/types queue payload and job-state contracts
workspace-scoped repository contract and Prisma schema
approved Stage 4 design system and shared component contract
representative website/PDF fixtures and isolated test services

serial_constraints: Freeze shared types before worker/web parallelization
Complete deterministic validation before candidate promotion
Complete frontend foundation before page composition
Serialize production-like integration and release validation

testing_strategy.strategy: Risk-weighted test pyramid with slice-local Vitest coverage, contract/integration checks at every merge gate, and Playwright launch-workflow validation before release.

test_levels.tool: Vitest plus Prisma test database and isolated Redis
Playwright keyboard/semantic checks plus manual screen-reader smoke

merge_plan.default: Validate each ticket, review shared contracts, merge in batch order
merge_plan.rollback: Revert batch merge or disable affected capability; never bypass a failed dependency gate

release_plan.release_strategy: Conservative staged rollout: internal integration environment, private alpha, controlled beta, then public readiness decision in Stage 7.

release_phases.name: Private alpha
release_phases.exit_gate: No critical defects; job/support signals reviewed

release_gates.name: Controlled beta candidate
criteria: Representative imports succeed within operational thresholds
No unresolved critical/high security or visual QA failure

release_gates.name: Public readiness
criteria: Accepted risks are current and owned

rollback_requirements: Versioned Prisma migrations with tested rollback/forward-fix choice
Web deployment rollback to previous Vercel deployment
Pause queues without losing job records
Preserve source artifacts and candidate data for replay
operational_readiness: support path for stuck jobs and import failures

stage_7_handoff_notes.deployment_preparation: Consume TICKET-021 build/deployment evidence; Stage 7 executes deployment and launch gates.

milestones.name: Foundation contracts frozen
exit_criteria: Clerk organization maps to workspace context
App shell and design tokens render responsively

milestones.name: Manual catalog and provider baseline demonstrable
exit_criteria: Manual item path works with zero AI providers
Provider health and routing states are visible

milestones.name: Import-to-catalog workflows demonstrable
exit_criteria: Website and PDF inputs create idempotent jobs
Partial failures and retries are visible
Bulk outcomes are per-record and recoverable

milestones.name: Private alpha release candidate
exit_criteria: Tenant isolation and credential checks pass
Responsive and keyboard evidence is registered
Rollback and operational checks are rehearsed

execution_risks.risk: Website scraping behavior and anti-bot variability can destabilize the core import slice.
execution_risks.mitigation: Build a narrow representative-site spike first; persist normalized artifacts; use idempotent per-category jobs and manual entry fallback.
execution_risks.next_action: Validate representative sites in TICKET-010 before broadening scraper behavior.

execution_risks.risk: Async job, worker, and UI status contracts may drift across web and worker workstreams.
execution_risks.mitigation: Freeze shared queue payload and job-state contracts in packages/types before parallel UI/worker implementation.
execution_risks.next_action: Review shared contracts at BATCH-002 merge gate.

execution_risks.risk: Tenant isolation or credential handling defects could expose workspace or provider data.
execution_risks.mitigation: Require workspace-scoped repositories, encrypted/server-only credentials, negative tenant tests, and security review before alpha.
execution_risks.next_action: Complete TICKET-003 and TICKET-019 before LAUNCH-GATE-001.

execution_risks.risk: Dense discovery and catalog interfaces may fail keyboard, responsive, or visual continuity requirements.
execution_risks.mitigation: Build shared accessible table/drawer patterns first and require preview, screenshot, keyboard, responsive, and design-system evidence.
execution_risks.next_action: Validate frontend tickets through TICKET-020 before beta.

execution_risks.risk: AI provider behavior and extraction quality vary while zero-provider operation remains mandatory.
execution_risks.mitigation: Keep provider adapters behind capability contracts, use deterministic validation, and test manual-only operation as a release gate.
execution_risks.next_action: Validate configured and zero-provider modes in TICKET-007 and TICKET-020.

coordination_notes: Freeze shared types before worker/web parallelization
Complete deterministic validation before candidate promotion
Complete frontend foundation before page composition
Serialize production-like integration and release validation

assumptions_made.assumption: Release through internal validation, private alpha, controlled beta, then public readiness review.
